name: Pakistan
shortSummary: India and Pakistan share a fraught relationship rooted in the 1947 Partition, the unresolved status of Jammu & Kashmir, and repeated wars. Formal trade and high-level diplomatic engagement have been largely suspended since 2019.
complexity: Four wars (1947, 1965, 1971, 1999 Kargil), cross-border terrorism, and the Kashmir dispute dominate the relationship. Diplomatic and trade ties were downgraded sharply after the 2019 Pulwama attack and India's revocation of Article 370.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Technical cooperation historically administered through the Permanent Indus Commission, now suspended.

majorChallenges.title: Kashmir dispute
majorChallenges.description: Unresolved territorial dispute over Jammu & Kashmir remains the central obstacle to normalization.

majorChallenges.title: Cross-border terrorism
majorChallenges.description: India cites Pakistan-based militant groups as a recurring source of attacks on Indian soil.

recentDevelopments.title: Pahalgam terror attack and Indus Waters Treaty held in abeyance
recentDevelopments.description: Following a terror attack in Pahalgam, India held the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, one of the most significant unilateral steps taken in the treaty's history.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Marked a sharp escalation, removing a decades-old mechanism that had survived multiple prior wars, and signalling a fundamentally more confrontational Indian posture.

recentDevelopments.title: Heightened military tension
recentDevelopments.description: Bilateral tension escalated further through 2025, with reports of cross-border incidents and international concern over the risk of wider conflict between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Underscores that the relationship remains the most volatile and dangerous in India's neighbourhood.

historicalEvents.title: Partition of British India
historicalEvents.description: India and Pakistan become independent states; Partition triggers mass migration and communal violence, and an unresolved dispute over the princely state of Jammu & Kashmir.

historicalEvents.title: Second Indo-Pakistani War
historicalEvents.description: War fought primarily over Kashmir, ending in a UN-mandated ceasefire and the Tashkent Declaration (1966).

historicalEvents.title: Indo-Pakistani War and Liberation of Bangladesh
historicalEvents.description: India intervenes in the Bangladesh Liberation War; Pakistani forces surrender in Dhaka, leading to the independent state of Bangladesh.

historicalEvents.title: Simla Agreement
historicalEvents.description: India and Pakistan agree to resolve differences bilaterally and establish the Line of Control in Kashmir.

historicalEvents.title: Kargil War
historicalEvents.description: Pakistani forces and militants occupy positions on the Indian side of the Line of Control in Kargil; Indian forces recapture the heights after weeks of fighting.

historicalEvents.title: Pulwama Attack and Balakot Airstrike
historicalEvents.description: A suicide bombing kills 40 Indian paramilitary personnel in Pulwama; India conducts airstrikes in Balakot, Pakistan, in response. Trade and diplomatic ties are downgraded sharply afterward.
historicalEvents.impact: India revoked Pakistan's Most Favoured Nation trade status; Pakistan suspended trade and downgraded diplomatic relations.

agreements.name: Indus Waters Treaty
agreements.description: World Bank-brokered treaty governing the sharing of the Indus river system; India held it in abeyance following the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

agreements.name: Simla Agreement
agreements.description: Post-1971 war framework committing both countries to bilateral resolution of disputes and defining the Line of Control.

trade.majorSectors: Formal direct trade largely suspended since 2019

multilateralRelations.detail: Both founding members, though SAARC summitry has been effectively frozen since 2016 due to bilateral tensions.
Frequently opposing positions, particularly on Kashmir at the UN Security Council and UNHRC.
